title: Clustered Integer Execution Core with Replicated Register Files
where_in_paper: Integer Execution Unit / Clustered Pipeline section
decision: Implemented a clustered integer execution core with two clusters (U0 and U1), each with its own replicated register file, execution units, and load/store unit, rather than a single unified integer core.
rationale: The paper's stated reasoning was to reduce wire delays and improve cycle time. Clustering allowed critical paths to stay within a cluster, reducing the need for long-distance communication. Results were broadcast to both register files to keep them consistent without explicit transfer instructions.
outcome: Two clusters (U0 and U1) each with an 80-entry register file (32 architectural, 40 rename, 8 PAL shadow), capable of issuing up to four instructions per cycle total.
weakest_point: The exact quote and page number are not available; the decision is well-documented in other sources but I am not 100% certain the paper explicitly frames it as a trade-off vs. a unified core.

title: Out-of-Order and Speculative Execution Pipeline
decision: Adopted an out-of-order and speculative execution pipeline, allowing instructions to execute as soon as operands are ready and to fetch/execute down predicted paths.
rationale: To maximize instruction-level parallelism and performance. Out-of-order execution starts critical path computations as soon as possible, and speculative execution extracts parallelism from branches.
outcome: A pipeline capable of fetching four instructions per cycle, with 80 in-flight instructions and an out-of-order issue queue.
weakest_point: The paper likely describes this as a given design choice rather than a debated decision with alternatives.

title: High-Bandwidth Memory System with Parallel Cache Access
decision: Designed a high-performance memory system with parallel access to on-chip and off-chip caches, and a high-bandwidth data path.
rationale: To quickly deliver data values to the execution core and provide robust performance for applications without cache locality.
outcome: A 64KB two-way set-associative instruction cache and a 64KB data cache, with many memory references serviced in parallel.
weakest_point: The paper's specific discussion of parallel access vs. alternatives is not confirmed from the abstract.

title: Aggressive 600 MHz Cycle Time in 0.35 µm CMOS
decision: Targeted and achieved a 600 MHz cycle time in a 0.35 µm CMOS process, maintaining Alpha's tradition of leadership clock frequencies.
rationale: To continue the Alpha tradition of an unequalled cycle time, facilitated by a clean RISC architecture and advanced design techniques.
outcome: A 500-600 MHz operating frequency, delivering 2.0-2.4 billion instructions per second.
weakest_point: The paper likely presents this as a result rather than a debated decision with trade-offs against lower frequency.

title: Integration of Advanced Branch Prediction (Tournament Predictor)
decision: Integrated a sophisticated two-level tournament branch predictor to support speculative execution.
rationale: To maximize performance by accurately predicting branch directions and enabling speculative execution down the predicted path.
outcome: A hybrid two-level branch predictor (tournament predictor) that enables high accuracy and performance.
weakest_point: The specific term 'tournament predictor' is widely associated with the 21264 but I am not certain it is detailed as a decision with alternatives in this specific IEEE Micro paper.
